children: Final August purchasing managers' surveys reaffirm the eurozone's resilience against various economic threats, Oxford Economics' Rory Fennessy says in a note. Despite higher gas prices denting disposable spending and some inventory-induced strength in the second quarter likely to unwind, some upside growth risks in the current quarter appear to be materializing, he says. "We will slightly upgrade our near-term GDP forecasts in our September forecast round," he says. The eurozone composite PMI was 52.0 in August, the same as July. "Manufacturing is showing little signs of unwinding the resilience shown throughout the second quarter, and while the improvement in services growth may have stalled somewhat, the sector remains in an overall healthy position," Fennessy says. (edward.frankl@wsj.com)
